from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Product Rule: The 'Teamwork' Formula", [
            "Product rule finds total change.", 
            "Functions f(x) and g(x) multiply.", 
            "Formula: f'g plus fg'."
        ])
        
        u = MathTex("u", color="#FFFF00")
        v = MathTex("v", color="#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(uv[0]), Indicate(uv[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Chain Rule", [
            "Chain rule: For composite functions.",
            "Analogy: Nested Matryoshka dolls.",
            "Derivative: Outer times inner derivative."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display nested function 'f(g(x))', #FFFFFF.
        comp_func = MathTex(r"f(g(x))", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(comp_func, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(comp_func))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight inner function 'g(x)' with color #FF00FF.
        # Note: MathTex objects can be tricky with indexing.
        # 'f(g(x))' -> [0]f, [1](, [2]g, [3](, [4]x, [5]), [6])
        # Indices for g(x) roughly [2:6]
        self.play(comp_func[2:6].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show chain rule formula: 'f'(g(x)) * g'(x)'.
        # Highlight multiplier 'g'(x)' in #00FFFF.
        formula = MathTex(r"f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'D3')
        
        # Pre-highlight inner derivative
        formula[4:8].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # Fade out everything except final formula.
        self.play(
            FadeOut(comp_func),
            FadeOut(self.lecture),
            FadeOut(self.title),
            formula.animate.move_to(ORIGIN)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Complex Application", [
            "Hybrid problem: Using both rules.", 
            "Wave function: Simplify and solve.", 
            "Step-by-step calculus application."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Hybrid problem: Using both rules.
        func_text = MathTex(r"f(x) = (x^2 + 1) \cdot \sin(x^3)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(func_text, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(func_text))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Wave function: Simplify and solve.
        # Highlight components: product #FFFF00, chain #FF00FF
        product_part = func_text[0][:7] # (x^2 + 1)
        chain_part = func_text[0][7:] # \cdot \sin(x^3)
        
        self.play(
            product_part.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            chain_part.animate.set_color("#FF00FF")
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Step-by-step calculus application.
        # Add arrows
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["B3"], end=self.grid["D2"], color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["B4"], end=self.grid["D4"], color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", ["Cheat sheet: Key formula summary.", "Product rule uses addition.", "Chain rule uses multiplication."])
        
        # Animations
        # Create cheat sheet checklist
        checklist = VGroup(
            Text("Summary Checklist:", font_size=24, color=YELLOW),
            Text("1. Product Rule: (uv)' = u'v + uv'", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
            Text("2. Chain Rule: (f(g(x)))' = f'(g(x))g'(x)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.place_in_area(checklist, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(checklist))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(checklist[1], color=YELLOW))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(checklist[2], color=YELLOW))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        success = Text("Success!", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(success, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(success))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Introduction: The Speed of Change (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly recap the power rule for simple derivatives (x^n). Introduce the 'Dynamic Duo' rules required when functions interact: Product Rule (multiplication) and Chain Rule (nesting).
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm: The Product Rule tracks the arm's total reach (length × angle), while the Chain Rule tracks the motor speed inside the gear mechanism.

sections.title: The Product Rule: The 'Teamwork' Formula (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain that when two functions multiply, f(x)g(x), the derivative isn't just the product of derivatives. It's 'derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times derivative of the second'. Use a graphic of two rectangles expanding.
sections.example: A squirrel gathering nuts: If the number of squirrels (f) increases while the nuts per squirrel (g) increases, the total rate of collection follows the product rule.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The 'Nested' Layers (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of composite functions f(g(x)). Use the 'Matryoshka Doll' (Russian nesting doll) analogy. The derivative is the 'outer derivative' times the 'inner derivative'.
sections.example: A rocket's height: The altitude depends on fuel (inner), and the fuel consumption depends on time (outer). Derivative = (change in height/change in fuel) × (change in fuel/change in time).

sections.title: Synthesis & Complex Application (3:30-4:30)
sections.content: Demonstrate a hybrid problem requiring both rules. Show how the visual graph of a complex wave simplifies when broken into its procedural parts.
sections.example: An animatronic character moving: Its arm extension is defined by f(g(x)) * h(x). Apply both rules step-by-step to calculate the instantaneous velocity.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Summarize with a visual cheat sheet. Product Rule (Addition of terms), Chain Rule (Multiplication of factors).
sections.example: Flashcard challenge: Quick identification of which rule applies to sin(x²) vs. x²sin(x).
